# Introduction

This assignment corresponds to Week 3 of the course, "Evaluation" (error measures, training/testing, cross-validation). You will build on the tract-level American Community Survey (ACS) data from HW_01 by merging it with a life expectancy dataset and using it to predict tract-level life expectancy. Along the way, you will pick an appropriate error metric for the outcome's distribution, and see how the same model's estimated accuracy, and whether adding geography to it looks like a good idea, can change depending on how you cross-validate.

The life expectancy data comes from the CDC's U.S. Small-area Life Expectancy Estimates Project (USALEEP), which estimates life expectancy at birth for individual census tracts from 2010-2015 mortality and population data. This fills a real gap: the federal government doesn't otherwise publish life expectancy below the county level, even though health outcomes can vary enormously from one tract to the next within the same county.

The regression itself is simple: each row is a census tract, the outcome is that tract's USALEEP life expectancy, and the predictors are the SoVI variables you built in HW_01 (poverty, health insurance coverage, income, education, and so on), plus, in Part 3 onward, a set of terms built from the tract's latitude and longitude. You're asking how much of a tract's life expectancy can be predicted from its socioeconomic profile (and location) alone, and how much you can trust your predictions.

## Preliminary Work

The steps below are preliminary work you will need to complete before you can complete the actual assignment. You do not need to document them in your HW_02 notebook.

### Step 1: Update your data pipeline

1. Copy the updated scripts from the `code` directory of this repository into your own repository, replacing your HW_01 versions and adding the two new ones (`01_build_data_dictionaries.py`, `02_download_data.py`, `03_build_sovi_variables.py`, `04_download_life_expectancy.py`, `05_merge_data.py`, `sovi_variables.py`, `census_config.py`, `run_all.sh`).
2. Delete everything in your local `data` folder. The output schema has changed, so you need a clean rebuild.
3. Re-run the scripts in order (or run `bash code/run_all.sh`). This will produce, among other files, `data/processed/sovi_tract_2024.csv`, `data/processed/sovi_tract_2015.csv`, and `data/processed/sovi_tract_2015_merged.csv`.

What the two new scripts do:

- **`04_download_life_expectancy.py`** downloads the census-tract-level life expectancy file from <https://ftp.cdc.gov/pub/Health_Statistics/NCHS/Datasets/NVSS/USALEEP/CSV/US_A.CSV> and saves it to `data/raw/`. This is the U.S. Small-area Life Expectancy Estimates Project (USALEEP); see <https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/usaleep/usaleep.html#life-expectancy> for background on how and when the estimates were produced.
- **`05_merge_data.py`** merges the **2015** tract-level SoVI data (not 2024: USALEEP's estimates are based on 2010-2015 mortality and population data using 2010 Census tract boundaries, the same vintage as the 2015 ACS data, while the 2024 ACS data uses the 2020 Census's redrawn boundaries) with the life expectancy data and each tract's centroid coordinates from the Census Gazetteer file, and builds a small set of polynomial terms from those coordinates. It produces `data/processed/sovi_tract_2015_merged.csv`, containing every SoVI variable, `life_expectancy`, and five geography columns (`geo_lat`, `geo_lon`, `geo_lat2`, `geo_lat_lon`, `geo_lon2`) for every 2015 tract. Tracts with no USALEEP estimate have a missing `life_expectancy` value rather than being dropped. You do not need to write any of this merging or feature-construction code yourself.
